text:
jen: Heads up — we need to finalize how gateway header overrides interact with console routing policies for model pinning. Current behavior is surprising to some tenants.

ravi: +1. Tenant reported that X-Model-Version header was winning over a console canary pin. Expected: console policy should take precedence for enterprise contracts.

alex: I remember we designed header overrides to be explicit opt-in for tenants. But console rollout pins were implemented later and we might have a precedence bug.

maria: Can you paste the request + rule chain? quick repro would help.

jen: Repro: tenant sends "X-Model-Alias: summarizer-v2" and platform console has a canary pin that routes 100% of that tenant to summarizer-v1 for now. Gateway currently routes to v2.

ravi: Hmm. Gateway evaluator applies rules in this order: route match -> header pins -> alias resolution -> console pins. Looks wrong. Should be: console pins -> header pins (if tenant has allowed overrides) -> alias resolution.

alex: Agreed. The policy engine currently treats headers as a higher-priority matcher because header matchers are evaluated on the raw request before consulting admin metadata. We can change evaluation order but need to audit all dependents.

jen: Proposed quick fix: introduce a "pinning.authority" flag on route config. Values: "console", "header", "tenant". Default is "console" for enterprise routes. Gateway will check authority precedence table before applying pins.

maria: That would be safe. Also add an allowlist: tenants can explicitly enable header-driven overrides in their tenant config if they want to self-serve. Without that, console/control-plane pins win.

alex: Implementation notes: small change in evaluator ordering. Pseudocode: 
```
for policy in ordered_policies(authority_precedence):
  apply(policy)
if pin_applied:
  short-circuit alias resolution
```
We need to persist authority_precedence per route and expose in console UI.

ravi: Telemetry: we should emit an event when a pin is overridden, including fields: route_id, tenant_id, applied_authority, requested_header, canonical_alias. This will let us detect regressions and misconfigurations.

jen: +1. Add console warning when a header override is configured but tenant-level allowlist is off. UX should surface that header was ignored.

ops-bot: NOTE: existing ruleset 0x7f3a will be re-evaluated when ordering changes are deployed. Expect ~3k re-eval ops.

maria: For rollout UX: we should introduce a toggle in the console per-route: "Respect tenant header overrides" with a tooltip explaining security and correctness implications. Default: off for enterprise routes.

alex: Security note: header overrides can be spoofed if proxies don't enforce auth. We should require a signed header (HMAC) for tenant override or only accept overrides on private endpoints.

jen: Good catch. Let's add requirement: header overrides require either mTLS or signed header. Add validation at gateway before applying.

dmitri: Regarding compatibility constraints: when console pins to an older model (v1) because of compatibility, header should not be able to force a newer model that breaks client contract. So authority_precedence must be aware of compatibility tags.

ravi: So final decision we propose to implement:
- Add route-level "pinning.authority" with default "console" for enterprise routes
- Allow tenant-level opt-in for header overrides in their account settings
- Require signed X-Model-Override header or mTLS for header overrides
- Emit telemetry event on any override/ignored header for audit/alerts
- Surface a console UX toggle and warning when header overrides are ignored
- Respect compatibility constraints: compatibility failures cause header overrides to be ignored (emit event)

jen: I'll open a PR for gateway evaluator + schema change and a console patch for the toggle. Will include rollback plan.

alex: Ping me on the PR for evaluator changes, I'll help with the tests.

maria: I'll prototype the small UX copy for the toggle and the tooltip.

ops-bot: deploy-bot triggered: dry-run eval of rule reordering completed for 2k routes, 12 mismatches flagged (see /links/dryrun-2356).

jen: Thanks all — timeline: aim to land evaluator change behind feature flag this week, console toggle next week, and then enable by tenant cohort.

ravi: One more: add a diagnostic endpoint "/internal/v1/pin-debug?route=...&tenant=..." that returns the evaluated policy chain and why a particular model was chosen (for oncall).

dmitri: +1 that will help SRE when customers file incidents. Make sure it redacts tenant secrets.

jen: Noted. I'll include the endpoint in the PR.

alex: Looks good. No objections from my side.

maria: LGTM.

jen: Closing thread after PR created. Thanks!
